name: Parkside Apartments (scattered site)
headline: Parkside Apartments is a 50-unit, fully Section 8-assisted family property at 1209 Tulip St in Longmont, which Lincoln Avenue Communities bought in December 2024. It is being re-syndicated and rehabbed with Mountain View Plaza, and won 2026 Federal 4% credits of $880,917 a year.
why_it_matters: It preserves 50 deeply subsidized two- and three-bedroom family homes, a scarce unit type, using bonds issued by the housing authority and a property tax exemption. The deal is a template for Longmont's other aging HAP properties.

status.label: Credits awarded; bonds and tax-exemption partnership approved; closing not confirmed
status.detail: Parkside shares one bond note and one SLP with Mountain View Plaza, both approved by LHA on 2026-06-16. The targeted 2026-08-17 closing and construction start has no confirming public record yet.

next_step: Watch LHA Board packets for the closing report, and City of Longmont building permits at 1209 Tulip St.

background.text: Lincoln Avenue Communities bought Parkside and Mountain View Plaza in December 2024 (about $27M combined, per BizWest). BizWest tags the Parkside buyer as Parkside Owner LLC.

The property is 100% covered by a HUD Section 8 HAP contract, and an existing LIHTC LURA restricts all units to 60% AMI or less. Comparable market rents cited are $2,270 for a two-bedroom and $2,450 for a three-bedroom.
Rehab scope (planned): energy and water upgrades, accessibility improvements, and updated units and common areas. Parkside's base hard cost line is $3,225,000.

Local deal: LHA (through LHA Ventures LLC) joins the owner partnership as a 0.01% special limited partner for 17.5 years. The property comes off the tax roll in exchange for an up-front fee and an annual PILOT, split with the city. LHA also gets a right of first refusal.
Bonds: LHA is the conduit issuer. Longmont's charter bars the city from issuing PABs without a vote, so the city assigns its cap to LHA instead. The single note covers both properties.
Affordability: new LIHTC LURAs will put about 25% of units at 30% AMI and all units at or below 60% AMI. The developer says this extends affordability at least 30 years.
The LHA Board vote on the first PAB inducement (LHA-2025-08) was 6-1. Every later LHA vote on the deal, and the city's R-2026-33, was unanimous.
LHA staff called the Parkside & Mountain View bond issuance, together with Atwood Commons, among LHA's first conduit bond issuances for a third-party project.
None of the city's 2026 PAB cap ($6,778,793) goes to this deal. The only 2026 letter of intent came from LHA itself (for 180 Emery Street).

discrepancies: CHFA prints $15,018,617 of PAB on both the Mountain View Plaza and the Parkside rows. LHA's resolution authorizes one combined note (not to exceed $16M) for both properties, so the figure is one issue, not $30M (chfa-4pct-award vs lha-res-2026-14).

CHFA's report also prints 'Longmont Housing Authority' and $15,018,617 on the 2025 '34th Street' row (Boulder, Boulder Housing Partners). That looks like a copy error in CHFA's report (inferred; chfa-4pct-award).
The one-time SLP fee is $476,488 in the February 2026 memo and worksheet, but $478,488 in the June 2026 memo (lha-memo-2026-02-17, lha-taxcalc-2026-02 vs lha-memo-2026-06-16).

The city's June 2026 council memo says all units would be restricted to 30% AMI or less (through the HAP vouchers). CHFA's award and the developer's application show LIHTC restrictions at 30% and 60% AMI, with about 25% of units at 30% (col-ccf-2026-06-09 vs chfa-4pct-award, lac-slp-app-2025-11).

The schedule slipped. The Nov 2025 application targeted an April 2026 construction start and December 2026 completion; the June 2026 LHA memo targets closing and construction start on 2026-08-17 (lac-slp-app-2025-11 vs lha-memo-2026-06-16).

The development budget carries $34.5M for acquisition, while BizWest reports about $27M paid in December 2024. The application says the existing ownership entities will sell to the new LIHTC partnership. That is a related-party resale at a higher (likely appraised) value; this is inferred (lha-budget-2026-02, lac-slp-app-2025-11 vs bizwest-2024-12-19).
The February 2026 budget lists CHFA upfront and ongoing issuer fees, although LHA ended up as issuer (lha-budget-2026-02 vs lha-res-2026-14).
